rubrics.criterion: The site record type decides itself whether it answers a requested domain name (the raw-file-name prefix convention), and no collaborator or endpoint compares a requested name against the record's file-name field anymore.
rubrics.rationale: Name matching was the most duplicated piece of the injected design: the lookup path and every mutation path re-implement the prefix convention from the record's raw file name. Moving this specific decision to the record is a distinct, greppable semantic outcome of this task, not a generic quality wish.

rubrics.criterion: The record performs its own on-disk operations as behavior: locating its file, loading its content, storing new content, deleting its file, and switching between the enabled and disabled encoding. No caller assembles a filesystem path from the record's directory and file-name data or performs the open/write/remove/rename directly on the record's behalf.
rubrics.rationale: All file conventions of the Nginx site layout (path composition, the '.disabled' suffix encoding, first-match deletion semantics) live in the collaborators' bodies in the injected state; asking which unit performs these specific operations is exactly the localization this task demands.

rubrics.criterion: A record obtained from the lookup path provides its content on demand, and the registry path no longer loads file contents into a record's field from the outside.
rubrics.rationale: The injected registry finder both matches and stuffs file contents into the record's content member; whether the loaded content now comes from the record (or an equivalent record-owned load) is an observable, independently checkable fact about one specific data member and one specific caller.

rubrics.criterion: The values the domains page renders per site (its display name, its contribution to the enabled list, and its modification-time card entry) are provided by the record, and the card assembly consumes those outcomes without splitting or slicing the record's raw file name at a distance.
rubrics.rationale: The injected overview builder re-derives names, enabled state, and timestamps from two of the record's data members; this is the read-side manifestation of the same relation and can be answered separately from the write-side outcomes.

rubrics.criterion: The callers are actually rewired onto the record-owned behavior end to end: the registry still turns the directory into records while skipping non-regular entries, the editor still sequences create/update/delete/state as coordinated operations, the overview assembly still produces the same grouping and ordering, and the endpoints route through the new shape without hand-rolled fallbacks to the old logic.
rubrics.rationale: A solver could add record-level behavior yet leave collaborators on their old inline paths; checking coordination completeness for these named operations is instance-specific and separate from whether the behavior exists at all.

rubrics.criterion: The repair is not a mechanical passthrough: the record's interface does not reduce to trivial per-field getters/setters (or one grab-bag convention-apply method taking a mode flag) that the collaborators still feed raw names and options into, while every actual convention decision — which suffix, which comparison, which rename — still lives in the caller.
rubrics.rationale: Blanket accessor generation is the cheapest uniform rewrite this instance invites, and a single parameterized apply-convention call is the second: both change spelling but not ownership, so the collaborators still hold the naming and state rules. This rubric exists to fail those specific evasions, which the deterministic checks cannot distinguish on their own.

rubrics.criterion: No dead residue of the migrated logic remains: the superseded path-building, matching, and state-splitting code is not left behind as unused helper methods or duplicated derivations inside the collaborators, and members and imports that lost their callers through the move are removed.
rubrics.rationale: The collaborators carry the old conventions in their bodies; a partial repair that layers record behavior on top without deleting the old inline derivations is a concrete, checkable leftover of this diff, not a generic style remark.

rubrics.criterion: The added behavior lives on the existing site record type itself, and no parallel record-shaped class or partially-populated duplicate of it is introduced to host the moved code.
rubrics.rationale: Splitting the domain object in two (one anemic, one rich) is a plausible-looking but wrong outcome here; the injected repository has exactly one record type, so this is an instance-specific structural fact that can be verified from the patch.

rubrics.criterion: Name resolution keeps its current tolerance: a request naming a strict prefix of a stored file name resolves on the read path and on the mutation paths exactly as before (for example, requesting a name that a longer file name starts with still selects that file), rather than becoming an exact-name or extension-aware comparison.
rubrics.rationale: The suite exercises full names almost exclusively, so a solver tightening matching to exact file names can pass every deterministic test while silently changing on-disk semantics; this negative fact protects the one resolution rule the task freezes.

rubrics.criterion: State handling keeps its edge semantics: activation removes exactly the final suffix of the record's file name regardless of further dots in the domain, operations keep working over freshly scanned records rather than reusing records mutated by earlier transitions, and enabling an already-active site keeps producing whatever file move the current implementation produces.
rubrics.rationale: Multi-label domains and repeated operations are where record-state repairs most often go wrong (splitting at the wrong dot, or caching a renamed record); these specific behaviors are stated as frozen in the task prompt and are independently checkable per operation.

rubrics.criterion: The on-disk footprint of each HTTP operation is unchanged: creation still writes a new site as a disabled file, content updates and state switches still apply to every matching file, removal still removes exactly one file and reports failure when none matched, and no operation touches files outside its current reach.
rubrics.rationale: Moving filesystem work into the record is precisely where eager redesigns alter behavioral reach (early-exit vs. all-matches, missing-file responses); these per-operation file effects are the concrete observable contract of this app, restated so a grader can check them one by one against the solver patch.
